name: Agricultural Communication & Media

objectives.text: Identify ways farmers, ranchers, and agricultural businesses share information with the public, such as farm tours, fair exhibits, newsletters, and social media
Distinguish facts from opinions in a news story, video, or post about farming or food
Describe the audience and purpose of different types of agricultural communication, such as a news release, a farm newsletter, or a social media post
Conduct an interview with a farmer or agricultural professional and report the findings in a short written article
Compare print, broadcast, and digital media as ways to reach consumers with information about agriculture
Identify distinctions among written agricultural communications, including news releases, newsletters, feature stories, opinion pieces, and blogs
Describe how agricultural organizations use verbal, written, and visual communication across platforms such as radio, photography, podcasts, websites, and social media
Write a news release in Associated Press style that reports an FFA chapter event or a supervised agricultural experience achievement
Apply principles of photography, layout, and graphic design to create a visual message about an agricultural topic
Analyze how media coverage of an agricultural issue, such as animal welfare or pesticide use, shapes public attitudes and behaviors
Explain the ethical and legal responsibilities of agricultural communicators, including accuracy, copyright, photo permissions, and farm privacy and biosecurity
Produce an agricultural radio segment, podcast episode, or short video that informs a target audience about an agricultural topic
Evaluate written agricultural communication pieces such as news releases, blogs, and social media posts for accuracy, clarity, and audience fit
Develop clear key messages that respond to a public misconception or controversy about agricultural production
Evaluate emerging digital communication tools, including generative AI, for their usefulness, accuracy, and ethical use by agricultural professionals and organizations
Develop a communications plan for an agricultural business, organization, or FFA chapter that defines purpose, target audience, message, media, and outcome evaluation

changes: Kept and reworded all six original objectives. Added distinguishing fact from opinion, interviewing and reporting, identifying written communication forms, describing platforms, writing an AP-style news release, visual design and photography, analyzing media influence, communication ethics and law, broadcast and podcast production, crisis and misconception messaging, and evaluating emerging digital tools including AI. Kept advertising, branding, and sales content out for sibling sub-topics. Mapped AFNR ECL standards to grade 9 to 12 objectives only.
